CLCON/284/2025
Rakesh Kumar & another
--Petitioners
 Versus
S N Pandey & others
--Respondents
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Dinesh Gahatori, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. J.S. Bisht, learned Standing Counsel along 
with Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, learned Brief Holder for 
the State.
3. The Division Bench of this Court passed the 
order dated 24.11.2023 in WPSB No. 591/2022, 
whereby the respondent-contemnor, Secretary, 
Revenue Department, was directed to take a decision 
on the Draft Rules submitted on 16.12.2021 within a 
period of six months from the date of the order 
passed by the Writ Court. Since the order has not 
been complied with, the present contempt petition 
has been filed.
4. Despite putting the respondents on notice, no 
compliance has been made with the order passed by 
the Division Bench even till today.
5. Learned counsel for the respondents￾contemnors submits that the matter has been placed 
before the Cabinet, but the Cabinet has adjourned 
the matter, despite the fact that the file was sent to 
the Confidential Section by the Board of Revenue. 6. This appears to be a clear violation of and non￾compliance of this Court's order dated 24.11.2023. 
The instructions, so-called, furnished by the 
respondent-contemnor are bereft of any merit.
7. Let the Secretary, Revenue Department, remain 
physically present before this Court on 07.09.2026, 
or comply with the order passed by the Division 
Bench.
8. List on 07.09.2026.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
01.09.2026 AK

CLCON/284/2025
Rakesh Kumar and Another
--Petitioners
 Versus
S. N. Pandey
--Respondent
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. Dinesh Gahatori, learned 
counsel for petitioners.
2. Mr. P.S. Bisht, learned C.S.C. with 
Mr. J.S. Bisht, learned Standing Counsel 
and Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, learned Brief 
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand/ 
respondent-contemnor.
3. Pursuant to order dated 07.09.2026, 
respondent-contemnor Mr. Surendra 
Narayan Pandey, Secretary (Revenue), 
is present before this Court.
4. Mr. P.S. Bisht, learned C.S.C. 
submits that the matter was placed, 
after the report received from 
confidential department, to the Cabinet 
and the matter was adjourned in the 
Cabinet.
5. This fact has already been brought 
to the notice of this Court by the 
petitioner and it is only thereafter this 
Court has passed the order for Secretary 
(Revenue) to appear before this Court to 
comply the order passed by writ court, 
wherein, draft rules have to be finalized. 6. The order of writ court is of the year 
2023 and the draft rules were of the 
year 2021, which have yet not been 
finalized. This is a very sorry state of 
affairs. It appears that the State 
Government is not serious with the order 
passed by writ court as the order passed 
by the writ court is still there and it has 
never been set aside by the superior 
court.
7. In such view of the matter, only on 
the assurance given by learned C.S.C. 
that he would discuss the matter with 
Mr. Shailesh Bagauli, Secretary to 
Hon’ble Chief Minister, the matter is 
adjourned for a week, so that learned 
C.S.C. would apprise this Court about 
the progress and the compliance of the 
order passed by writ court to avoid the 
unpleasant situation.
8. Put up on 18.09.2025.
9. The presence of respondent￾contemnor Mr. Surendra Narayan 
Pandey, Secretary (Revenue), is 
exempted till further orders.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 09.09.2026
PN
